classDescriptions.stable: Stable mangrove. NDVI follows the seasons, but its long-term level stays high and does not change much.
classDescriptions.gain: Gain. NDVI rose by 0.3 or more between the first and the last 3 years of the record, for example through mangrove growth or regrowth.
classDescriptions.loss: Loss. NDVI fell by 0.3 or more between the first and the last 3 years of the record.
classDescriptions.loss + recovery: Loss and recovery. Mangrove (NDVI 0.3 or more) at the start and the end, but NDVI was below 0.3 for at least two years in between.
classDescriptions.high turnover: High turnover. NDVI moves up and down strongly, with at least a whole year below 0.25 or a lot of back-and-forth change, without one clear direction.
classDescriptions.non-mangrove: Non-mangrove. NDVI stays low: below 0.3 at the start and the end and below 0.25 on average, for example water, bare soil or salt flats.

pointDescription.breakpointRule: A breakpoint is an abrupt change of at least {threshold} NDVI within 12 months, after which the new level persists for at least 2 years.
pointDescription.ews: Before the drop, we calculated the standard deviation, AR1, kurtosis and skewness of NDVI to look for early warning signals: {verdict}.
pointDescription.verdictEws: an early warning signal was found (AR1 and standard deviation both rose significantly)
pointDescription.verdictNoEws: no early warning signal was found
